note: Uncited, and I could not evidence it anywhere. Worse, it invents a menu item: no source mentions a vegan karaage at Mokumoku. The documented savoury items are a toast set, a quiche set and a seasonal vegetable curry. Drop the karaage reference; the generic soy-sauce caution can stay only if reworded to name real dishes.

quote: The kitchen has been fully vegan since September 2025, with no animal products on the menu, so the risk of animal-derived cross-contact is low by design. Plant milks (oat and soy) are available for drinks.
found: Vegan cafe and art gallery. Menu includes lunch sets, gluten-free sweets and drinks. Reported September 2025 to be fully vegan. ... 2 fully vegan set menus available. Oat and Soy milk for beverages.
method: r.jina.ai text proxy on both sites
note: Both facts - fully vegan since September 2025 and the oat/soy milks - are on HappyCow, not on FMGF. FMGF only tags 'Vegan options' and never mentions September 2025 or plant milks. Repoint the citation.

quote: Staff are described as friendly and the food as made with care, and menu items are labelled as vegan/gluten-free, but no specific allergy-handling protocol is documented in the sources.
found: playing jazz music in a cosy environment with a very friendly staff ... we ordered a drink and a sweet each which said they were plant-based and specifically written that no egg or milk is used
note: Supported, and the page is genuinely silent on allergy protocol. Caveat: the article is from June 2023 and its opening hours (Wed-Sat 9:00-15:00, Sun 11:00-15:00) already disagree with HappyCow (Tue-Sat 8:30-15:00, closed Sun and Mon).

quote: Reviewers consistently praise the gluten-free tofu donuts and gluten-free set as very good.
found: The tofu donut was very unique and I loved the slightly chewy texture. / Nice lunch sets, including a gluten free set that was very good.
note: Well supported across several reviews on HappyCow and again on FMGF (tofu donuts were the best thing ever). One 2025 review notes 'Limited menu, no lunch set anymore' - the GF set may not always be available.

quote: Fully vegan kitchen with clearly labelled items and seasonal, house-made cooking; the philosophy is that vegan and gluten-free should not mean compromising on taste.
found: Just because it's vegan and gluten-free does not mean you have to compromise on taste or quality!
note: Two problems. (1) The quoted philosophy is the travel blogger's own exclamation about her lemon muffin, not the cafe's stated philosophy - stop attributing it to the venue. (2) The same article calls Mokumoku 'a vegetarian cafe' whose lunches 'all look vegan, but it would be best to confirm', so it cannot support 'fully vegan kitchen'; that comes from HappyCow's September 2025 report. Seasonal house-made cooking IS supported here.

quote: record metadata: vegan_status 'full', vegan_label 'Fully vegan / veg'
found: Vegan cafe and art gallery ... Reported September 2025 to be fully vegan.
note: Correctly flagged. One older HappyCow review lists a con of 'Not entirely vegan', but that predates the September 2025 change.

found: 18 recent ratings ... Gluten Sensitive / 2 days ago / Nice cafe with 3 types of donuts and muffins.
note: Trading - FMGF review two days old; HappyCow shows current hours Tue-Sat 8:30am-3:00pm. Address consistent across sources (87 Hoshinocho, Higashiyama Ward, 605-0853).

quote: Utsuwa to Cafe Bar Mokumoku
note: Two unsupported claims (an uncited soy-sauce line naming a vegan karaage that no source shows, and a 'no source documents a dedicated fryer' line the record's own FMGF source refutes) plus two citations pointing at the wrong site. The venue itself looks better than the record says.

quote: This branch carries the same chain menu as MOS Burger Japan-wide, including the low-allergen sealed-pack rice-burger and hot dog, which are prepared and sealed off-site to limit allergen contact. No location-specific cross-contamination protocol is documented for the open kitchen, so confirm handling with staff on the day.
found: Low Allergen Menu / Pork Burger <Rice Flour> ... Pork Hot Dog <Rice Flour>
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + tag strip; then the linked allergy PDF via pdftotext
note: The cited inbound page is chain marketing (What is MOS BURGER, how to order, Teriyaki/Tonkatsu flavours) and never mentions low-allergen items, sealed packs or rice buns. Also fix the wording: the item is a 'Pork Burger <Rice Flour>' - a burger with rice-flour BUNS. MOS's separate 'MOS Rice Burger' line is a different product and is NOT gluten-free; calling this a rice-burger could send a celiac to the wrong item.

quote: MOS publishes an English allergen list (PDF) and notes that ingredients can vary by store and that information is not fully guaranteed, so celiac diners should rely on the sealed low-allergen items rather than the standard menu.
found: The products may come into contact with ingredients that are not used in the product or mixed into the products at the factory or the store. Some ingredients may change depending on the store. Please understand that the information is not completely guaranteed.
note: Supported almost word for word, and current. The PDF adds a stronger line worth surfacing: 'Please consult your doctor in advance and purchase under your own responsibility.'

quote: MOS's signature Teriyaki Burger sauce is built on Japanese teriyaki, which is made with soy sauce that typically contains wheat - so the regular burgers, sauces and most of the standard menu are not celiac-safe.
found: 1973 May: The new hamburger "Teriyaki Burger", a major hit, is introduced
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + full-text grep for soy/wheat/gluten/allergen
note: ALARMING CITATION: this is MOS's 1972-1989 corporate milestone timeline. It records the year the Teriyaki Burger launched and nothing else - no soy sauce, no wheat, no allergens, no ingredients of any kind. A wheat-in-soy-sauce safety claim is resting on a corporate history page. Re-source to the allergy PDF (per-item wheat column) or to the Alle Hapi line about allergens hiding 'even in soy sauce'.

quote: A vegetable burger (MOS Yasai Burger) is on the menu, but it is not certified vegan and is prepared in a shared kitchen alongside meat and dairy items; standard sauces and buns may contain egg, milk or animal-derived ingredients. Vegans should ask staff to check ingredients and preparation.
found: MOS Yasai Burger / MOS Yasai Burger Double Patty / Soy Patty MOS Yasai Burger
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + allergy PDF
note: The inbound page lists no Yasai Burger and says nothing about vegan status. The allergy PDF does carry MOS Yasai Burger and its Soy Patty variants, and its blanket contact warning supports the shared-kitchen caution. Repoint.

quote: The chain-wide low-allergen rice-burger and hot dog are certified gluten-free and free of wheat, egg and milk, and arrive in sealed plastic packaging - a rare reliable option for celiac and multi-allergy diners at a burger shop.
found: Allergy friendly menu does not use egg, milk, wheat, shrimp, crab, soba and peanut as their ingredients. ... Since their every product is packaged individually, there is no chance for any allergens to get into the package at the store.
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + full-text grep of the allergy PDF for 'certified' / 'gluten'
note: ALARMING WORDING: 'certified gluten-free' appears nowhere - not on Alle Hapi, not in MOS's allergy PDF, which says the opposite ('the information is not completely guaranteed'). The items are formulated without wheat, egg and milk and are individually sealed; that is not certification. For a celiac reading this app that is exactly the wrong word. The rest of the sentence is fine once 'certified gluten-free' is removed and 'rice-burger' is corrected to rice-flour bun.

quote: MOS provides an allergen list in English and cooks each item fresh to order, which can make it easier to ask about and confirm ingredients.
found: * Allergy List available in English. ... You will get a number. Please wait for a little while, we only cook food after receiving your order.
note: Both halves verbatim on the cited page ('Everything is made to order' too). The one claim on this record that its cited URL genuinely carries.

quote: is the business still trading?
found: Allergies Information ... updated August 4th 2026
note: Chain-level sources are current (allergen list updated 4 Aug 2026, inbound site copyright 2026) and both low-allergen items are still listed. I could not verify the individual Nijo Station outlet from the cited sources - no branch-level page is cited for either MOS record.

quote: MOS & CAFE - Nijo Station
note: Only one of six claims is carried by the URL it cites. Two point at the chain's inbound marketing page, which covers none of the low-allergen or vegan content attributed to it; one rests on a 1970s corporate history timeline; and one asserts a gluten-free certification that no source makes.

quote: This is a wheat-noodle ramen shop, so it should be treated as NOT celiac-safe. Even the vegan ramen is explicitly made with whole-wheat (zenryufun) noodles, meaning every bowl on the menu contains wheat. No gluten-free noodle or dedicated gluten-free preparation is documented.
found: 【ヴィーガン】メニュー 京野菜香る塩栄養全粒粉麺使用 2000円 / とんこつ風野菜栄養全粒粉麺 2000円 / ヴィーガン100％信州味噌栄養全粒粉ラーメン 2000円
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA; then Yahoo Japan search on the shop name, which surfaced a Find Me Gluten Free listing the record does not cite
note: The whole-wheat noodle detail is verbatim, but the last two sentences are FALSE. Find Me Gluten Free (biz/ramen/6074142037770240) documents gluten-free noodles for an extra 800 yen and a gluten-free miso soup base, with the owner showing diners the packaging. The record is running on a December 2023 blog post and telling celiacs there is no GF option when there is one. Add the FMGF source - and its warnings, which are the real safety story.

quote: Wheat noodles are sourced from a noodle maker (Kiyokawa Seimen in Chichibu); the same noodle pots and broths serve all bowls, so cross-contamination with gluten is effectively unavoidable for a strict celiac diner.
found: この麺は埼玉県秩父の製麺所「清川製麺所（きよかわせいめんじょ）」のものを取り寄せているそうです。
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + r.jina.ai on the FMGF listing
note: The noodle maker is verbatim (Kiyokawa Seimenjo, Chichibu, SAITAMA - the record omits the prefecture). The shared-pot half is not in the blog at all; it is evidenced on FMGF by celiac reviewers: 'Not safe for celiacs. They use the same water for regular and GF noodles and there is soy sauce in the soup base' and 'They have gluten free noodles, but they're cooked in the same water as regular noodles.' Another reviewer got the noodles cooked in separate water on request. Cite FMGF for this.

quote: The salt-based bowls are seasoned with 'white tamari' (shiro-tamari), a naturally brewed seasoning from Iga, Mie. White tamari is typically brewed mostly from wheat, so it should be assumed to contain wheat/gluten unless the shop confirms otherwise.
found: 「（塩）フランス ブルターニュ地方のゲランド塩」または「（醤油）三重県伊賀市の本樽仕込みの天然醸造白たまりなど」のカエシ
note: ALARMING INVERSION: the page assigns these the other way round. The SHIO (salt) bowls use Guerande sea salt from Brittany; the SHOYU bowls use the naturally brewed white tamari from Iga, Mie. The record hangs a wheat warning on the wrong half of the menu - which for a celiac choosing between shio and shoyu is exactly backwards. FMGF independently confirms 'there is soy sauce in the soup base'.

quote: A dedicated vegan ramen is on the menu (including a 100% vegan Shinshu-miso version and a 'tonkotsu-style' vegetable bowl), and the shop reportedly gets frequent vegan inquiries from international visitors. However, the broths for the regular menu are made from chicken bones, pork and bonito/dashi, and there is no documented separation of cookware or noodle water, so vegan diners should confirm how the vegan bowl is cooked relative to the meat and fish broths.
found: ヴィーガン100％信州味噌栄養全粒粉ラーメン / とんこつ風野菜栄養全粒粉麺 ... 名古屋コーチンと大山鶏ガラをベースに香味野菜・昆布・鰹節で抽出したスープ ... 白湯は名古屋コーチンと大山鶏ガラと茨城豚がベース
note: Menu items and the chicken/pork/katsuobushi broths are all verbatim. Two corrections: there are THREE vegan bowls, not the two the record's vegan_detail claims; and 'the shop reportedly gets frequent vegan inquiries from international visitors' is an embellishment - the article only says the area has many foreign tourists so vegan was put on the menu.

quote: A genuine, clearly labeled vegan ramen is part of the standard menu, and the shop is used to fielding vegan questions from overseas guests - a good sign for being able to discuss dietary needs.
found: メニューは「鶏清湯・鶏白湯・伊勢海老白湯・ヴィーガンラーメン」など。外国人観光客が多いエリアなのでヴィーガンもメニューにありました。
method: plain fetch, iPhone UA + HappyCow and FMGF via r.jina.ai
note: The first half is fine. The second half is invented - the article never says the shop fields vegan questions, only that vegan is on the menu because the area draws foreign tourists. Easy repair with real evidence: HappyCow calls them 'three clearly labeled types of vegan ramen' and FMGF reviewers repeatedly say 'Owner very friendly speaks good English' and that he showed them the GF noodle packaging.

quote: record metadata: vegan_status 'full', vegan_label 'Fully vegan / veg', category 'VEGAN', vegan_detail 'two vegan ramen options'
found: 精選ハムと生ハムラーメン 塩or醤油 1300円 / 特選神戸牛ラーメン 塩or醤油 3850円 / 伊勢エビ（半匹）ラーメン 5850円 ... トッピングは ... 京豚で作ったレアチャーシュー ... 伊勢海老白湯ラーメンの場合は海老のテリーヌ

HappyCow classifies it 'Serves meat, vegan options available'. vegan_status must be 'options'; category 'VEGAN' is wrong; and there are three vegan bowls, not two.

note: The GF label is actually CORRECT but uncited, and it directly contradicts the record's own prose ('No gluten-free noodle ... is documented'). Add this FMGF listing to the record and carry its caveats: shared noodle water by default, soy sauce in the soup base, no dedicated fryer, but separate-water cooking granted on request to a diner who then had no reaction.

Three unsupported claims, including a straight inversion of which broth carries the wheat-brewed seasoning, plus a fully-vegan tag on a shop selling prosciutto and Kobe beef ramen.
